question: What is the main difference between community nutrition and clinical nutrition?

options.A: Intravenous feeding protocols for hospital patients
options.B: Dietary practices within entire population groups
options.C: Surgical management of severe gastrointestinal disorders
options.D: Prescription drug therapy for metabolic conditions

explanation: Community nutrition focuses on the health and diets of entire populations rather than individual patients in a hospital. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h1)

question: Why do primary health care nurses in Nigeria need to look beyond individual diets when managing malnutrition?

options.A: Hospitals lack the resources to record individual dietary histories
options.B: Malnutrition often stems from broader social and economic factors
options.C: Clinical guidelines require physicians to handle all meal planning
options.D: Government policy prohibits nurses from counseling single patients

explanation: Widespread nutritional issues are frequently driven by community-level challenges like poverty and living conditions, not just personal choices. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h1)

question: A community nurse connects a severely malnourished child to an Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP). What core duty is the nurse performing?
explanation: Guiding vulnerable patients to specialized centers for care falls under referral and coordination duties. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h2)

question: What is the main public health goal of a community nurse conducting outreach in a local market?

options.B: Providing practical health education and dietary demonstrations
options.C: Enforcing municipal tax laws on food vendors

explanation: Market outreach brings health education directly to where community members buy and prepare their food. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h2)

question: Which measurement is most helpful for quickly screening toddlers in areas with limited resources?
explanation: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) tapes are portable, fast, and effective for field screening without needing heavy scales. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h3)

question: Which clinical sign helps distinguish kwashiorkor from marasmus?
explanation: Kwashiorkor features fluid retention and swollen feet (edema), whereas marasmus is pure wasting without prominent edema. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h4)

question: A toddler presents with sparse discolored hair, skin peeling, and swollen feet. What condition should the nurse suspect?
explanation: Swollen feet, hair changes, and skin lesions are classic signs of kwashiorkor. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h4)

question: Why do top-down nutrition programs often fail in rural communities?

options.A: Rural residents refuse to accept any form of external assistance
options.B: They frequently ignore local food preferences and economic constraints
options.C: They rely exclusively on expensive imported medical equipment
options.D: Government regulations forbid community members from participating

explanation: Programs must fit local cultures and realities to gain community acceptance and succeed. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h5)

question: When teaching mothers how to prepare weaning foods using local crops in Nigeria, which ingredients should the nurse prioritize?

options.A: Affordable local staples like soybeans and groundnuts
options.B: High-sodium processed snacks and canned goods
options.C: Synthetic vitamin powders without local food bases
options.D: Imported commercial formulas from overseas markets

explanation: Using accessible, protein-rich local crops ensures mothers can easily prepare the meals at home. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h5)

question: Which teaching method is generally most effective for changing nutrition practices in a community?

options.A: Reading lengthy academic medical journals aloud
options.C: Interactive cooking demonstrations and visual aids

explanation: Practical, hands-on demonstrations engage learners better than abstract lectures or dense texts. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h6)

question: What is the best approach when a mother shares a harmful traditional dietary belief during a counseling session?

options.A: Validate positive habits while gently correcting myths
options.B: Publicly reprimand her to discourage others from listening
options.C: Ignore the comment and continue reading the lecture notes
options.D: Discontinue all future health education sessions immediately

explanation: Respectful dialogue builds trust and makes people much more open to changing their behavior. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h6)

question: Which partner helps the community nurse promote backyard gardening and crop diversification?
explanation: Agricultural workers have the farming expertise needed to support community garden projects. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h7)

question: Why is it important to involve religious and traditional leaders in community nutrition programs?

options.A: It secures community entry and cultural endorsement for campaigns
options.B: They are legally required to sign off on all nursing budgets
options.C: They act as primary clinical diagnosticians for malnutrition
options.D: It prevents the government from auditing local health clinics

explanation: Local leaders hold great influence over community trust and active participation. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring ongoing community nutrition programs?

options.A: Punishing staff members for missed administrative targets
options.B: Eliminating the need for any future community research
options.C: Permanently closing clinics that fail to show profit
options.D: Tracking routine data to ensure goals are being met

explanation: Monitoring gives regular feedback on how well a program is running and if it is making progress. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h8)

question: How does operational research benefit public health nutrition nursing?

options.A: It identifies emerging nutritional threats so policies can adapt proactively
options.B: It eliminates all cultural barriers to food distribution instantly
options.C: It guarantees that funding will never decrease in any circumstance
options.D: It replaces the need for direct patient contact and bedside care

explanation: Research helps nurses and health planners stay ahead of changing health trends and challenges. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h8)
